article.dek: Inactives are in, the storm cleared the field but not the rain, and the total kept falling — the last word before kickoff at MetLife.

items.headline: Lead: inactives are in — Burks and Okonkwo play, Skattebo and McCarthy play, and the only surprise is a Giants cornerback sitting
paragraphs: The inactives landed about 90 minutes before kickoff, and there are no surprises on the Washington side. Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) are out, exactly as the final injury report said. Nick Allegretti starts at center against the Giants' pass rush.

The good news held too. Wide receiver Treylon Burks is active after missing the Rams game with a foot injury, and tight end Chig Okonkwo is active as well. Washington's receiver group is whole for tonight.

The Giants have two names to know. Linebacker Malik Harrison — the only player on either team with a designation other than out, questionable with a groin injury — is inactive. Cornerback Paulson Adebo is inactive too, and that one is a demotion, not an injury: he started the season as one of the team's top three corners, and Colton Hood takes his place. On the good side, running back Cam Skattebo plays after missing one game with a hamstring injury, and J.J. McCarthy starts at quarterback.
items.takeaway: Burks and Okonkwo are active for Washington, Patrick and Yankoff are out as expected, Harrison is inactive for the Giants, Adebo sits as a demotion, and Skattebo and McCarthy both play.

items.headline: Injuries: Drew Lock is throwing again, and Seattle's left tackle is back at practice
paragraphs: Sunday's quarterback picture got a little steadier on Thursday. Drew Lock was limited again with the elbow and oblique injuries, but he resumed throwing, and he is still the starter with Sam Darnold ruled out. Darnold did not practice again with his ribs and quad injuries and is targeting a return in Week 12, after Seattle's bye.

The other Seattle name matters just as much. Left tackle Charles Cross practiced for the first time since his Week 7 ankle injury, working as a limited participant. He has missed the last two games. The Seahawks issue their designations for Sunday's game in Las Vegas on Friday.
One warning that has not changed: the app board still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter. It has not caught up to any of this. Do not trust the board's quarterback names for Sunday.
items.takeaway: Lock resumed throwing and stays the starter with Darnold out until Week 12, Cross is back at practice for the first time since Week 7, and the board still lists Darnold as the starter.

items.headline: Weather: severe weather cleared the field, warmups resumed, and kickoff stayed on time
paragraphs: The storm made its own pregame show. Lightning in the area forced the players off the field and the fans out of the seating bowl around 6:35 p.m. ET, with everyone told to take shelter inside the stadium. Warmups resumed at 7:24 p.m. ET after about a 30-minute delay, and the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff stayed on schedule.

The rain itself is not going anywhere. The final forecast has showers before midnight and rain after midnight, a low around 44, a north wind at 9 to 15 mph with gusts as high as 25 mph, and a 90% chance of rain. It will be wet all game.
Say it plainly, same as this morning: this is a forecast fact, not a totals edge. Rain alone does not make a bet.
items.takeaway: Lightning cleared the field and stands around 6:35 p.m. ET, warmups resumed at 7:24 p.m. ET, the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff stayed on time, and rain is forecast all game with gusts to 25 mph.

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — Thursday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the board after the evening refresh. It is the same board as this morning — generated November 2, still showing Week 8, now ten days old. The only game with a market board is Bears at Seahawks, played November 2.

So the headline cards are still from a finished game, and they must not be bet. For the record, they read: Hit Rate on the Seahawks moneyline at -175, Balanced and Value both on the Bears +3 at -102. Those games are done. Do not bet those cards.

Here is how to read them anyway, because the same three cards will be back when the board flips. Hit Rate is the pick most likely to win. Balanced is the strong pick without paying too much. Value is always the model's +EV play. Hit Rate is not worse for not being +EV. It is a different job: most likely to win.

Until the board flips, tonight's game has no card at all. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, ten days old, still showing last week's Week 8 cards — it still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter and knows nothing about tonight — so the Commanders-Giants price goes through Check.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Learn the Game: the hook — the half-point that decides a bet
paragraphs: The hook is the half-point on a spread. It sounds tiny. It decides bets all the time.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say one book has a team at -2.5 and another has the same team at -1.5. If the team wins by exactly 2, the -1.5 cashes and the -2.5 loses. That half-point — the hook — is the whole difference between a win and a loss on the same team, in the same game.

That is why shopping matters. A -1.5 is a genuinely better price than a -2.5 on the same team, and the hook is the reason. When two books disagree by a half-point, take the better number — and run it through Check before you bet it.
items.takeaway: The hook is the half-point on a spread — win by exactly 2 and a -1.5 cashes while a -2.5 loses — so when books disagree by a half-point, the better number is worth shopping for.

items.headline: The total fell again — 41.5 to 40.5 — while the spread held at Giants -2.5
paragraphs: The total kept sliding through the day. DraftKings has it at 40.5 now, down from 41.5 on Wednesday evening and 44.5 when it opened. The spread did not move: the Giants are still -2.5, with the moneyline at Giants -142 and Washington +120.

One number is still sitting there for the taking. FanDuel has the Giants -1.5 — a full point better than DraftKings' -2.5 on the same team. FanDuel's total is 41.5, and Circa and Pinnacle have it at 41. A -1.5 is a genuinely better price than a -2.5, and the hook is the reason: win by exactly 2 and the -1.5 cashes while the -2.5 loses.

The public is on the Giants, and the money agrees with the crowd. VSiN reports the Giants drawing more than three-quarters of the bets as the line moved from -1.5 to -2.5, and DraftKings is reporting 69% of the spread bets and 63% of the moneyline bets on New York. Tickets and handle on the same side is not a Fade — nothing in the market is arguing against the move. And the board still has not caught any of this. Tonight's game is not on the board at all, so run Check on your book's number.
items.takeaway: The total fell to 40.5 at DraftKings from 41.5 on Wednesday evening and 44.5 at open, the spread held at Giants -2.5, FanDuel's -1.5 is a full point better, and the public and the money agree on the Giants — no verified split argues against the move.

items.headline: Thursday's lesson for Sunday: get your number before the rush
paragraphs: Tonight is decided. The designations are in, the inactives are in, the forecast is final, and the line has already moved twice this week — the Giants went from -1.5 to -2.5 while people waited, and the total fell four points. The only thing left to learn tonight is the final score.

So take the lesson into Sunday. The final designations land Friday, and inactives come about 90 minutes before kickoff. If your book has a good number now and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number on Sunday, because waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too — and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams pushes lines past the app's playable number.
items.takeaway: Tonight's wait is over — the designations, inactives, forecast, and line moves are all in — so for Sunday, if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now instead of waiting for the Sunday rush to move it against you.
